metadata.title: norm_spectrum
metadata.description:
Initial public release of norm_spectrum, a lightweight Python package for normalization of astronomical spectra.

Included in v1.0.0

  • pseudo_norm: broad running-median continuum / pseudo-continuum normalization for 1-D spectra.

  • Suitable for quick analysis tasks such as spectral plotting and radial-velocity measurements.

  • Behaves as a conventional continuum normalization for spectra with a well-defined continuum, and as a pseudo-continuum normalization for strongly structured or line-blanketed spectra.

  • Continuum window can be specified either in wavelength units or directly in pixels.

  • Optional propagation of formal uncertainties.

  • Wavelength-unit agnostic.

  • Handles unsorted wavelength arrays and preserves invalid input flux samples.

  • Importable directly with:

    from norm_spectrum import pseudo_norm

  • Installable with pip install ., or usable directly from a directory on PYTHONPATH.

  • Requires only NumPy and SciPy.

The package is structured to accommodate additional normalization routines in future releases.
metadata.notes: If you use norm_spectrum in your work, please cite the software release.

metadata.title: hamop: bands, DOS, Kubo optical conductivity and NEGF transmission from one tight-binding Hamiltonian
metadata.description:
Local spectroscopy release: the NEGF layer now answers where in a device the spectral weight sits and how the current flows through it, not only how much transmits.

New in hamop.negf

  • device_greens: the retarded device Green function G(E) of the partitioned two-probe system (leads folded in through their Sancho-Rubio self-energies), the quantity every local observable below is built from -- returned with the broadening matrices, so users can construct their own correlators.
  • device_ldos: the site- and orbital-resolved local density of states from the spectral function A = i(G - G+), overlap (nonorthogonal) bases included.
  • bond_currents: the energy-resolved bond-current map J_ij of Paulsson and Brandbyge (Phys. Rev. B 76, 115117 (2007)) for carriers injected from either lead -- the microscopic current paths whose cuts recover the Landauer transmission.

Anchors (asserted in the tests, not stated)

  • The finite-eta spectral identity i(G - G+) = G (Gamma_L + Gamma_R + 2 eta S) G+ holds to machine precision -- overlap matrix included -- so the LDOS is exactly consistent with the same Green function the transmission uses.
  • A closed device reproduces the exact closed form: its LDOS equals the sum of eta-Lorentzians over its own eigenvalues, site weights included.
  • On a translation-uniform ribbon the LDOS is exactly uniform along the transport direction.
  • Bond currents obey Kirchhoff's law at every interior site to machine precision; every transverse cut through the device carries exactly the transmission T(E); injection and drain contacts source and sink exactly +T and -T.
  • Inside a band gap every bond current vanishes.

124 closed-form-anchored tests across Python 3.9-3.13. Install: pip install -U hamop.
metadata.notes: If this software is useful in your work, please cite it.

metadata.title: Campus-Scale 5G NR Radio Propagation Dataset: Processing and Application Code
metadata.description: This software accompanies the dataset “A Campus-Scale 5G NR Radio Propagation Dataset Integrating Drive-Test Measurements, 3D Environmental Geometry, and Ray Tracing.” It provides Python workflows for drive-test measurement preprocessing, coordinate alignment, Sionna RT base-station parameter calibration, per-station radio-map generation, network-scale best-server radio-map construction, measurement–simulation matching, physical base-station localization, sparse radio-map reconstruction, and visualization. The software is designed for use with the associated dataset released through Mendeley Data.

metadata.title: UniScFlow: public-accession reconstruction and guarded remapping of single-cell RNA-seq raw data
metadata.description: UniScFlow is a Python and shell workflow for reconstructing mapping-ready inputs from public single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq accessions. It validates project and run scope, integrates repository metadata with direct inspection of raw-read streams, infers platform and logical read roles, constructs canonical mapper inputs, and routes supported projects to STARsolo or STAR plus featureCounts. Recognized cases without a validated automatic mapping route terminate with an explicit, machine-readable unsupported or resource-dependent stop instead of claiming a count matrix. This frozen v1.0.0 deposit contains the software distribution only; public sequencing data and validation outputs are not included.

hits.title: UniScFlow: public-accession reconstruction and guarded remapping of single-cell RNA-seq raw data

metadata.title: SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC) — research artifact
metadata.description:
The complete experiment framework behind the PoPETs 2027 paper SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC).

It contains implementations of every reconstruction attack in the paper's taxonomy, including the six the paper introduces (CoBP-RA, CondMST, CondDDPM, CondRePaint, ARFFormer, MultiHeadMLP); the composable chaining and ensembling wrappers; the synthetic-data-generation layer covering all nine evaluated generators plus four further differentially private mechanisms used for the epsilon sweep; and the rarity-weighted reconstruction-advantage scoring code that was also the official NIST Collaborative Research Cycle metric.

It also ships results.db, a SQLite database of all 49,126 scored attack runs behind the paper, together with reproduce.py, which regenerates the paper's tables and figures from it. DATABASE.md documents that database for use as a standalone dataset, independently of this framework.

Evaluation is four CPU-only commands in a provided Docker image; ./test.sh verifies the environment end to end in about two minutes. No GPU is required.

Note on this archive: automatically generated source archives do not include git submodule contents. The external/recon-synth and external/MIA_on_diffusion directories will be empty here. Everything needed for the paper's tables, the test suite and the reduced-scale experiments works without them; only the diffusion attacks and LinearReconstruction require them. To obtain those, clone with git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/steveng9/Reconstruction.git.

hits.title: SoK: Reconstruction Attacks on Synthetic Tabular Data (Insights from Winning the NIST CRC) — research artifact

metadata.title: Title: Gradient-power compactons reproducibility code, data, and figures
metadata.description: Reproducibility source code, numerical data, and generated figures for computations on gradient-power compactons. The archive contains symbolic verification scripts, static and spectral numerical checks, padded Fourier-Galerkin time-integration code, Jacobi-Galerkin generator diagnostics, numerical CSV datasets, and generated reproducibility figures. The included scripts and data provide the numerical and computational material required to reproduce the reported calculations and figures.

metadata.title: cohort-harmonise: dictionary-first harmonisation and claim auditing across youth-development cohorts
metadata.description:
A dictionary-first harmonisation tool for aligning constructs across five longitudinal youth-development cohorts — LSAC (Growing Up in Australia), ABCD, TESS (Trondheim Early Secure Study), Ten to Men and LSIC (Footprints in Time) — using variable-level metadata only, with no access to participant data and no redistribution of dictionary files.

Cohorts and target constructs are configuration rather than code, so the tool generalises to constructs and cohorts beyond the anxiety application it was built for. Four adapters cover the dictionary shapes encountered, including inventories built from published documentation for cohorts with no custodian codebook; every row records the tier of evidence it rests on, distinguishing a custodian dictionary from a published cohort profile from a reconstruction assembled from methods sections.

Outputs: a construct coverage matrix over primary waves; a register of constructs declared non-harmonisable, each with a mandatory stated reason and empirical confirmation of absence; an assessment, for every cohort pair, of whether genuine common items exist to anchor a multi-group latent model or whether the inference must be harmonised instead of the scale; a check that the cohorts holding a construct agree on who reported it; and an audit of published methodological claims against the cohorts' own dictionaries.

Verdicts are evidence-tier aware. A cohort read from a custodian dictionary can contradict a claim; a cohort inventoried from publications can only fail to confirm one, and is reported as unverifiable rather than false. A declared absence is confirmed only for cohorts where a dictionary exists to confirm it in.

Data governance is enforced in code rather than described in prose: a governed cohort is excluded unless explicitly included, its culturally grounded wellbeing indicators cannot be mapped as standing in for a diagnostic construct, and a non-harmonisable declaration without a stated reason raises an error. Provenance records a SHA-256 over every dictionary read, so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases without those files being redistributed.

creators.name: Wichstrom, Lars
creators.affiliation: Norwegian University of Science and Technology, Trondheim, Norway

metadata.notes: No participant data is read, produced or redistributed by this software: it operates on variable-level metadata only, and no cohort dictionary file is included in this archive. Reproducing the reports requires obtaining each dictionary from its custodian under that study's own terms; docs/data_sources.md lists the expected paths and sources, and outputs/provenance.json records a SHA-256 over each file read so a third party can confirm they ran against the same releases. One cohort is governed under the CARE Principles for Indigenous Data Governance and the Maiam nayri Wingara Indigenous Data Sovereignty Principles; it is excluded from the published outputs unless sign-off is documented.

hits.title: cohort-harmonise: dictionary-first harmonisation and claim auditing across youth-development cohorts
